text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswana press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The president has retired High Court judges Barrington Jones and Taufik Cortran who have reached the age of 70.

- The Basarwa bushmen are seeking an interview with President Ketumile Masire to protest against plans to move them from their traditional villages in the Central Kalahari game reserve to make way for a tourist and wildlife development.

- Legislation to compel courts to hear rape cases in camera came into effect on Friday. The law also covers indecent assault cases and defilement of minors. The media are also prohibited from naming the victims.

- Management of the BCL Limited copper mine at Selibi-Phikwe says it is concerned at sulphur dioxide fumes from the mines polluting the town, but adds it is constrained by the high cost of alternative technology.
